title: Request-level token stitcher for SLA and billing reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a robust way to correlate low-level per-token timings and KV cache interactions back to the originating customer request for SLA reconciliation and usage billing. Current token probes produce dense telemetry that is useful for aggregate dashboards but cannot reliably account for cross-request cache reuse or micro-batched execution that splits a single logical request across multiple runtime slices.

Goals: build a "stitcher" pipeline that reconstructs request->token sequences with cache-hit annotations and assigns compute/time cost to the initiating request. The system should: 1) attach minimal request-scoped metadata at ingest (correlation id, prefix hash), 2) merge micro-batch token spans into logical sequences, 3) annotate tokens with cache-hit vs compute attribution, 4) produce per-request token-cost and latency breakdowns usable by billing and SLA teams, and 5) support sampling knobs to limit telemetry volume.

Constraints: must not increase p99 request latency by more than 3% when probes are enabled, storage budget for high-cardinality traces is limited (we target 30% additional disk for first-year retention), and integration must be compatible with both hosted and Dedicated runtimes.

Approach: implement lightweight correlation headers emitted by the API layer (x-rd-request-id, x-rd-prefix-hash). Enrich token probes at runtime with these headers when present. Introduce a stitcher service that consumes token-span events from the metrics pipeline (Kafka) and emits reconstructed request-level events to the observability warehouse and billing queue. Use a tolerant merge algorithm to handle out-of-order micro-batch fragments and mark partial reconstructions. Implement cache-hit inference by correlating KV-cache access logs with token spans and embedding a hit/miss flag on tokens. Provide a sampled full-trace mode for debugging and an aggregated mode for billing where only totals are stored.

Success metrics: accuracy of per-request token cost vs ground truth within 1% on synthetic workloads; end-to-end ingestion latency under 2s for reconstructed request events; telemetry overhead <3% p99 latency regression; billing pipeline adoption in pilot customers (at least 2).
acceptance_criteria: Correlation headers added to API (x-rd-request-id, x-rd-prefix-hash) and documented in SDK
Runtime token probes include request id and prefix hash when present
Stitcher service reconstructs >99% of requests in synthetic workload and emits per-request totals
Cache-hit annotation validated against KV access logs with >98% precision
End-to-end pipeline latency for reconstructed events < 2s at 1k req/s sustained
Telemetry sampling knobs exist (1%, 10%, 100%) and default to 10% for hosted users
Billing queue receives per-request token cost format and test invoices match ground truth within 1%
Security review completed and schema approved for PII-safe telemetry
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Chen: Ticket created after roadmap sync; flagged as important for Q1 billing parity. Added initial goals and constraints.
2025-02-20 Liam O'Connor: Drafted correlation header RFC and pushed to confluence. Initial API change scoped to add x-rd-request-id and x-rd-prefix-hash with backward compat toggle.
2025-02-27 Design review: UX team suggested including an optional human-readable request label for troubleshooting; decided to make it opt-in to avoid PII exposure.

2025-03-02 Eng sync: Prototype stitcher implemented consuming token spans from kafka.topic 'token-spans-v2'; basic merge algorithm handles out-of-order fragments up to 5s window. PR opened: runtime#1284 and observability#462.

2025-03-04 QA: Synthetic workload run shows reconstruction accuracy 99.3% at 500 req/s; cache-hit precision initially 92% due to delayed KV log joins. Work in progress to include per-access sequence IDs from KV layer.

2025-03-06 Liam O'Connor: Blocker identified - the logging schema change required for KV access sequence ids needs ops approval for Dedicated customers. Created ops ticket ENG-95210 to coordinate rollout plan.
